To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the absorption rates of the organic electrolytes are directly proportional to their lipid solubility, the absorption rates of organic acids are directly proportional to the lipid solubilities of their unionized species, and the absorption rates are directly proportional to concentration.
the absorption of 7- methylsulfinyl-xanthone-2 carboxylic acid from the respiratory tract is slower than that of 7-(m ethylthio)xanth one-2-carbox ylic acid.
the absorption rate of organic acid and its sodium salt are controlled by their lipid solubility, and that the absorption rate is inversely proportional to their molecular weight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of dosage regimen for bronchoconstrictive drugs.
the design of dosage regimens for bronchial administration of new drug entities and the formulation of inhalation aerosols.
designing the inhalation aerosol formulation of a drug entity with a desired pharmacologic activity and with a desired rate of systemic absorption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pulmonary absorption of a drug entity depends on the physicochemical properties of the compound, such as the lipid solubilities, ionization, and particle size of the compound.
a drug entity intended for inhalation therapy should be administered as an aerosol containing an aqueous solution or suspension of the drug entity in a pH range near its pKa.

the pulmonary absorption of organic electrolytes and organic acids from the respiratory tract is a complex function of the pH and concentration of the drug solution, the lipid solubilities of the unionized drug species, and the pKa of the drug.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pulmonary absorption of organic acids or organic electrolytes is directly related to their lipid solubility.
a dosage regimen for a new drug entity intended for inhalation aerosol therapy can be designed by studying the absorption of the drug entity from the lung model in situ.
, for a given drug entity, the pulmonary absorption is directly related to the concentration of the unionized drug entity in the dosage form.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pulmonary absorption is mainly determined by the physicochemical properties of the drug and the dosage form.

the absorption rates of the drugs from the respiratory tract are directly proportional to the concentration and that the absorption rates are controlled mainly by the lipid solability of the unionized drug species.

we can now use the rat lung model for in situ absorption studies in the design of dosage forms intended for the treatment of pulmonary diseases and the design of dosage regimens for prophylactic and therapeutic use.
